annotations.title: Buscar empresas com um sinal agora

description: Finds, now, companies of a market that show a buying signal, with one decision maker at each, and saves them in a sheet before it returns: a signal's daily monitor as a one-off list, with the same search, checks, kept answers and prices. category is the signal: hiring (open job posts: Nock's job index first, then the job boards; market.hiringTitle is the role), funding (rounds raised, each confirmed by a second source before it is delivered), news (news about the company: a kind of news or what happened, in the Brazilian press), job_change (people new in a role, at a new company or promoted: the person found is the decision maker, no lookup), erp (companies that run an ERP, proved with public evidence), cnpj (from the Receita through the Nock Registry: event opening = empresa nova, branch = filial nova, by industry or CNAE, place and periodDays 7/30/45/60/90; every event but opening needs a state or an industry; a branch has a CNPJ and no site), site_tech (tools the company's own site and e-mail domain load, e.g. HubSpot, RD Station: technologies and change uses, adopted or removed), tech (one tool by name; a tool the site shows, asked as presence, is read on the site as site_tech; any other comes from job posts and detections) and loyalty_club (supermarkets, by their main CNAE, checked for a loyalty club: filter sem_clube or clube_concorrente, location a state or a city). market takes the same fields as that signal's monitor (tech: technology, detectionMode, periodDays, location; online stores by their platform are not searched here). rules (hiring, news, cnpj) keep only the companies that meet them, each row checked charged. It also looks up one decision maker at each company (jobTitle, default "CEO, Sócio, Diretor"; area "financeiro" keeps only finance decision makers; decisionMakerFallback role_only, the default when jobTitle or area is given, leaves a company where nobody holds the role without one and says so (decisionMakerNotFound), partner accepts the Receita's managing partner with their LinkedIn looked up, 3 credits only when found; findPeople false skips it; withEmail adds the work e-mail) and writes the planilha única: the company with the signal, its one-line finding, its public source and address, the decision maker as a person row of that company. sheetId adds to an existing sheet and skips the companies it already has (they are neither searched nor charged again); without it a sheet named sheetName (default the signal and what it looks for) is reused or created. limit 10 by default, 200 at most. Two steps: without confirmed it runs nothing, charges nothing and returns maxCredits, the most the call can cost, with the prices; with confirmed true it runs and charges. Prices, as each monitor: hiring 4 credits per company delivered (8 when the paid job board found it); funding 4 per company (24 when the paid source found the round); news 4 per company; job_change 4 per person; 2 per row checked against rules, passed or not; erp 6 per company delivered with the ERP proved (its check and the job post read for it included; the ones checked and left out are never charged); cnpj 2 per company; site_tech (and tech read on the site) 4 per company delivered and 2 per site read now and not delivered (a reading kept from the last hours is free); tech from job posts 24 per company; loyalty_club 4 per supermarket delivered (the supermarkets checked and not delivered are free); 8 per decision maker found by search (a partner the Receita names is free); 3 per work e-mail found. Finishes within about 85 seconds and returns the companies (name, domain, facts of the finding, evidence source and url, decision maker), counts, creditsCharged, sheetId and sheetPath; erp also returns the funnel (funnelText) and the candidates per source, and takes market.companies to check a list. partial true means the time ran out or a source failed before the limit was reached; "more" says how to continue (the same input with the returned sheetId brings the next companies).

area.description: Optional: only decision makers of this area ("financeiro" keeps finance people and leaves out titles such as "Controller Jurídico"); without jobTitle it also looks for the area's titles.

category.description: The signal: hiring, funding, news, job_change, erp, cnpj, tech, site_tech, loyalty_club (and any other the description lists).

confirmed.description: false or absent: returns the most it can cost and runs nothing. true: runs and charges.

decisionMakerFallback.description: When nobody holds the role asked: role_only (the default when jobTitle or area is given) leaves the company without a decision maker and says so; partner accepts who decides there (the managing partner the Receita names, free, or the owner the business engine finds), with their LinkedIn looked up by name and company. Without jobTitle and area, partner.

findPeople.description: false brings only the companies, no decision maker. Default true.

jobTitle.description: Who to find at each company, titles tried in order, comma-separated. Default "CEO, Sócio, Diretor".

limit.description: Companies to bring, 10 by default, 200 at most.

market.description: The market of that signal, with the same fields as that signal's monitor market (category may be left out). hiring: hiringTitle (required), location, seniority, companySizes, industry, rules; funding: periodDays (7, 30, 90 or 180), location, companySizes; news: periodDays (7, 30 or 90), categories or what, location, rules; job_change: jobTitle, periodDays (30, 60 or 90), location, industry, companySizes, move; erp: erps, hiringArea, location, industry, companySizes; cnpj: event (opening = empresa nova, branch = filial nova, or another registry event), periodDays (7, 30 or 90), industry, location (every event but opening needs a state or an industry), fiscalSizes, revenueMin, revenueMax, rules; tech: technology (one tool), detectionMode (presence or first_seen, default presence), periodDays (7, 30 or 90, default 90), location; site_tech: technologies (tools the site loads, e.g. hubspot, rdstation), change (uses, adopted or removed), location, industry, companySizes, or domains (the customer's accounts); loyalty_club: filter (sem_clube or clube_concorrente), location (a state or a city).

sheetId.description: An existing sheet to add the companies to; companies already in it are skipped and not charged. Without it, a new sheet is made.

sheetName.description: The name of the sheet to use or make when there is no sheetId (a sheet of that name is reused).

withEmail.description: Also look up each decision maker's work e-mail. Default false.
